assessment_summary: The relation 'X beats Y' (P(X > Y) > 1/2) is not transitive, as demonstrated by the existence of non-transitive random variables. A counterexample is constructed where X beats Y, Y beats Z, but X does not beat Z.
counterexample: Let X, Y, Z be independent random variables defined as follows: X=3 with probability 1; Y=2 with probability 2/3 and Y=5 with probability 1/3; Z=1 with probability 1/3 and Z=4 with probability 2/3. Then P(X>Y) = P(Y=2) = 2/3 > 1/2, so X beats Y. Next, P(Y>Z) = P(Y=5) + P(Y=2)P(Z=1) = 1/3 + (2/3)(1/3) = 5/9 > 1/2, so Y beats Z. But P(X>Z) = P(Z=1) = 1/3, which is not > 1/2. Thus X does not beat Z, disproving transitivity.
